learning_science_pillars.name: Retrieval Practice (Prática de Recuperação Ativa)
learning_science_pillars.authors: Roediger, H. L., & Karpicke, J. D. (2006) / RetrievalPractice.org
learning_science_pillars.schedule_policy: Quizzes diagnósticos imediatos pós-leitura e flashcards ativos sem consulta prévia
learning_science_pillars.aquila_implementation: Geração automática de drills L1/L2/L3 exigindo recuperação ativa da memória antes de exibir pistas.

learning_science_pillars.name: Spacing Effect / Curva de Ebbinghaus (Prática Espaçada)
learning_science_pillars.schedule_policy: Ciclos determinísticos de revisão em 24h, 48h, 96h e 144h baseados em acurácia observada
learning_science_pillars.aquila_implementation: Agendamento adaptativo de revisões sem prometer percentuais fixos irreais de retenção.

learning_science_pillars.name: Interleaving (Prática Intercalada de Conceitos)
learning_science_pillars.schedule_policy: Alternância entre tipos distintos de problemas (ex: Geometria + Álgebra + Física) na mesma lista
learning_science_pillars.aquila_implementation: Evita resolução mecânica por bloco repetitivo, treinando a discriminação de qual estratégia aplicar.

learning_science_pillars.name: Mastery Learning (Aprendizagem para o Domínio)
learning_science_pillars.authors: Bloom, B. S. (1968) / Khan Academy / Kumon Method
learning_science_pillars.schedule_policy: Bloqueio de avanço até atingir domínio verificado dos pré-requisitos granulares
learning_science_pillars.aquila_implementation: Árvore de pré-requisitos Kumon (L1 -> L2 -> L3) com aprovação de diagnóstico antes de liberar o próximo tópico.

learning_science_pillars.name: Cognitive Load Theory (Teoria da Carga Cognitiva)
learning_science_pillars.schedule_policy: Segmentação em micro-passos, eliminação de redundância e uso de Exemplos Resolvidos (Worked Examples)
learning_science_pillars.aquila_implementation: Decomposição de questões complexas de ENEM/ITA/PISA em passos atômicos com Worked Examples.

learning_science_pillars.name: Dual Coding Theory (Dupla Codificação Verbal + Visual)
learning_science_pillars.schedule_policy: Integração simultânea de explicação textual concisa + diagrama vetorial SVG + simulação PhET
learning_science_pillars.aquila_implementation: Vinculação de cada questão difícil a um ativo visual SVG em `research_visual_assets`.

learning_science_pillars.name: Self-Explanation Effect (Autoexplicação Guiada)
learning_science_pillars.schedule_policy: Solicitar que o estudante justifique o 'porquê' de cada etapa antes de revelar o gabarito comentado
learning_science_pillars.aquila_implementation: Prompts SFT socráticos que pedem a justificativa conceitual do aluno antes da resposta final.

learning_science_pillars.name: Formative Assessment (Avaliação Formativa Contínua)
learning_science_pillars.schedule_policy: Feedback imediato, específico e de baixo risco focado no erro conceitual (misconception) detectado
learning_science_pillars.aquila_implementation: Mapeamento explícito de `misconceptions` e `hints` em cada item do banco normalizado.

resources.subject: Physics / Física
resources.topic: Newton's Laws of Motion & Free-Body Diagrams
resources.learning_objective: Apply Newton's second law (ΣF = m·a) to multi-body coupled systems on inclined planes with kinetic friction
resources.content: Two blocks of masses m1 = 4.0 kg and m2 = 6.0 kg are connected by a massless string over a frictionless pulley on a 30° incline (μk = 0.20). Determine the system acceleration and string tension.
resources.solution: 1. Decompose weight of m1: Fg1x = m1·g·sin(30°), Fn1 = m1·g·cos(30°), fk = μk·Fn1. 2. Write ΣF = (m1+m2)·a -> m2·g - m1·g·sin(30°) - μk·m1·g·cos(30°) = (m1+m2)·a. 3. Solve for a = 3.24 m/s² and T = m2(g - a) = 39.4 N.
hints: Identify all forces acting on each block separately
Draw a Free-Body Diagram (FBD) with axes parallel and perpendicular to the incline
misconceptions: Using sin(θ) instead of cos(θ) for the normal force on an incline
resources.attribution: Urone, P. P., & Hinrichs, R. OpenStax College Physics 2e, CC BY 4.0

resources.subject: Chemistry / Química
resources.learning_objective: Identify the limiting reactant and calculate theoretical and percent yield in chemical reactions
resources.content: When 25.0 g of N2 reacts with 5.00 g of H2 to form NH3 (N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3), determine the limiting reactant and the maximum mass of ammonia produced.
hints: Convert all reactant masses to moles first
Divide moles of each reactant by its stoichiometric coefficient
misconceptions: Assuming the reactant with the smaller mass in grams is automatically the limiting reactant
resources.attribution: Flowers, P., Theopold, K., & Langley, R. OpenStax Chemistry 2e, CC BY 4.0

resources.subject: Biology / Biologia
resources.learning_objective: Explain how the proton-motive force across the inner mitochondrial membrane drives ATP synthesis
resources.content: Explain the effect of an uncoupling agent (such as 2,4-DNP) that makes the inner mitochondrial membrane permeable to H+ ions on oxygen consumption and ATP production.
resources.solution: The proton gradient dissipates without passing through ATP synthase, halting oxidative phosphorylation (ATP drops), while the electron transport chain runs maximally, increasing O2 consumption and releasing energy as heat.
hints: Separate electron transport (pumping H+) from chemiosmosis (H+ flowing back through ATP synthase)
misconceptions: Believing O2 is directly converted into CO2 during the citric acid cycle
resources.attribution: Clark, M. A., Douglas, M., & Choi, J. OpenStax Biology 2e, CC BY 4.0

resources.subject: Mathematics / Matemática
resources.topic: Functions, Domain, Range & Rate of Change
resources.learning_objective: Determine the average rate of change and domain restrictions of composite and rational functions
resources.content: Find the domain and average rate of change of f(x) = sqrt(2x - 6) / (x - 5) on the interval [3, 11].
resources.solution: Domain requires 2x - 6 >= 0 (x >= 3) and x != 5, so [3, 5) U (5, inf). On [3, 11], note discontinuity at x=5; for g(x)=sqrt(2x-6), Δg/Δx = (sqrt(16) - 0)/(11 - 3) = 4/8 = 0.5.
hints: Check both radical non-negativity and denominator non-zero conditions
misconceptions: Forgetting to exclude points where the denominator equals zero inside the radical domain
resources.attribution: Abramson, J. OpenStax Precalculus 2e, CC BY 4.0

resources.learning_objective: Ensure 100% prerequisite mastery before unlocking multi-step problem solving
resources.content: 4-step mastery ladder: Attempted -> Familiar (70%+) -> Proficient (100% unit quiz) -> Mastered (mixed unit test after spacing delay).

resources.license: Public Domain / OECD Open Educational Assessment Framework
resources.subject: Mathematics, Science & Reading Literacy
resources.topic: Real-World Quantitative Modeling & Scientific Evidence Evaluation
resources.learning_objective: Formulate, employ, and interpret mathematics and scientific evidence in complex real-world contexts
resources.content: PISA Released Item Pattern: Given carbon emission curves and vehicle fuel efficiency data across two decades, evaluate whether a proposed municipal tax policy achieves a 30% reduction target.
resources.solution: Calculate fleet-weighted emission totals before and after policy implementation, accounting for total fleet growth (+18%) vs per-vehicle reduction (-22%), proving net reduction is only 7.96% (< 30%).
hints: Distinguish per-capita/per-vehicle rate from total aggregate volume
misconceptions: Confusing a percentage reduction in rate with a reduction in total absolute emissions when population grows
resources.attribution: OECD / NCES Program for International Student Assessment (PISA) Released Items

resources.subject: Mathematics & Science (Grades 4 and 8)
resources.topic: Cognitive Domains: Knowing, Applying, and Reasoning
resources.learning_objective: Diagnose 4th and 8th grade student proficiency across Knowing, Applying, and Reasoning cognitive domains
resources.content: TIMSS Grade 8 Reasoning Item: A metal ring is heated uniformly. Does the inner diameter of the hole increase, decrease, or stay the same? Explain microscopically.
resources.solution: The inner diameter INCREASES. Thermal expansion scales all linear dimensions equally (like a photographic enlargement) as interatomic distances increase.
hints: Imagine heating a solid disk first, then ask what happens to a circle drawn inside that disk
misconceptions: Believing the metal expands inward into the hole and makes the hole smaller
resources.attribution: IEA / NCES TIMSS Released Assessment Questions

resources.source: MIT OpenCourseWare & MIT Open Learning Library
resources.subject: Physics, Calculus, Computer Science & Chemistry
resources.topic: MIT 8.01 Classical Mechanics / 18.01 Single Variable Calculus / 6.0001 CS
resources.learning_objective: Solve olympiad and engineering-level mechanics and calculus problem sets with analytical rigor
resources.content: MIT 8.01 Problem Set: A spool of mass M, inner radius r, and outer radius R (moment of inertia I_cm) rests on a rough horizontal table. A string wound around the inner radius is pulled at angle θ. Find the critical angle θ_c for which the spool slips without rolling.
resources.solution: Torque about instantaneous point of contact P vanishes when the line of action of tension T passes through P -> cos(θ_c) = r / R.
hints: Take torque about the contact point with the ground to see which way the spool tends to rotate
misconceptions: Assuming friction always points opposite to the applied horizontal pull in rolling bodies
